summary: Stuart McFarlane worked in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Lancaster University, including in the Department of Religious Studies, attested in 1991 and 2001.

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was a scholar in archaeology and Indology. He studied at Churcher's College, University College London, and the UCL Institute of Archaeology under Mortimer Wheeler (~1934–1936), and held a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).

Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under David M. Knipe (completed 2001) and held a post at Oregon State University (attested 2018).

Su Bai (1922–2018) was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as professor there from 1948 to 2004.

Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) studied at Chulalongkorn University, UCL, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and University of London. An archaeology scholar, he held posts at Silpakorn University as dean (1964) and rector (1976–1986), and directed SEAMEO SPAFA (~1987–1992).

Subhash Kak (born 1947) studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan. Working in Indology and engineering, he held professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

Subrata K. Mitra (born 1949) studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. He held academic posts at the University of Hull (~1980–1989), University of Nottingham (~1989–1994), University of Heidelberg (~1994–2014), and NUS (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan (born 1941) is a scholar of history and archaeology. She studied at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the University of California, Berkeley, and became an emerita professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1990).

Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) studied at Gujarat University, Mannheim, Vienna, and the Sigmund-Freud-Institut. Working in Indology and religious studies, he held posts at IIM Ahmedabad (~1971–1975) and IIT Delhi (1976–1977), alongside visiting roles at institutions including INSEAD.

Sudhākara Dvivedī (1855–1910) was an Indology and history scholar who studied under Devakrishna. He served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as librarian (1883), mathematics and astrology teacher (1890), and professor and head of mathematics (1898–1905).

Sue Hamilton is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and held an academic post at King's College London (attested 2001–2003).
Suehiro Tanemura (1933–2004) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He later held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1971–1978) and Kokugakuin University (~1978–1998).

Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukhlal Sanghvi (1880–1978) studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra. Working in Indology and philosophy, he taught at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922) and held the Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944).

Sukra Sagar Shrestha (1956–2018) was an epigraphist and scholar in archaeology and Indology. He held epigraphist posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986) and Nepal's Department of Archaeology (attested 1987).

Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) studied at Burdwan Raj College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and I. J. S. Taraporewala. A linguistics and Indology scholar, he became lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (1954) at Calcutta.

Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She served as professor of English at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and taught at Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an engaged Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Assumption College and the University of Wales, Lampeter, and served as editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand (~1963–1969).

Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania. Working in history and Indology, she held faculty posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–1999) and the University of Michigan (~1999–2007).

Sumi Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert Buswell (attested 2014).
